courses.title: Agricultural Water Resource Management
courses.description: Water resource management applied to current issues. Water delivery systems in the United States and California, survey of water rights, water pollution, water conservation, food and agricultural system water use, and efficient water management. Includes water problems in developing nations.

courses.title: California Water
courses.description: [GE 4C] Review of the history of the water system and water policy in California, including the major social, political, and environmental issues. Introduction to water law for non-lawyers and applies concepts of sustainability to water policy.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Basic Irrigation Science
courses.description: An introduction to irrigation methods, such as drip, micro, surface and sprinkler for nursery, landscape, runoff, field crops and tree plant crop irrigations. Basic soil-plant-water relationships. Information needed for planning, designing, and scheduling of an irrigation system, irrigation hydraulics, irrigation efficiencies, and modern controllers.

courses.title: Introduction to Turfgrass Management
courses.description: The grasses, materials, and techniques involved in the maintenance and management of all types of athletic and recreational fields. Corequisite(s): PLT 2400L .

courses.title: Introduction to Turfgrass Management Laboratory
courses.description: The grasses, materials, and techniques involved in the maintenance and management of all types of athletic and recreational fields. Corequisite(s): PLT 2400 .

courses.title: Computer Aided Design
courses.description: Introduction to computer-aided drafting/design intended for irrigation system design and other horticultural applications. Basic CAD commands, tools, multi-view drawing and dimensioning techniques. Corequisite(s): PLT 2520L .

courses.title: Computer Aided Design Laboratory
courses.description: An introductory course in computer-aided drafting/ design intended for irrigation system design and other horticultural applications. Basic CAD commands, tools, multi-view drawing and dimensioning techniques. Corequisite(s): PLT 2520 .

courses.title: Sprinkler/Drip Irrigation
courses.description: An introduction to sprinkler and drip micro-irrigation systems and techniques. Systems will be discussed that apply to landscape and agronomic crops. Water savings and management will be a major part of this course.

courses.title: Construction I: Site Engineering and Landscape Construction
courses.description: Explores fundamental technical theories, concepts, methods and processes associated with engineering and constructing the built landscape. Emphasis is placed on site engineering, water management, tectonic structure and project construction workflow.

courses.title: Pesticide Laws and Regulations
courses.description: Federal and California Laws and Regulations affecting individuals, corporations, and agencies providing for the public health, safety and welfare; and protecting the environment including our natural resources. Emphasis on hazardous materials, ground water protection, pesticides, and pest control laws and regulation. Pesticide safety included. Function and structure of pertinent federal, state and county agencies and their enforcement practices as they relate to agribusiness, public health and pest control operations, including case studies.

courses.title: Landscape Contracting and Estimating
courses.description: Management of landscape contracting firms. Bonding, insurance, contracts, ownership, licensing and other legal aspects of improvement to real property. Calculation of costs, manpower, and quantities of materials in landscape development. Preparation of specifications and estimates used in bidding. Corequisite(s): PLT 4160L .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 131 or PLT 1120 ; and PLT 131L or PLT 1120L .

courses.title: Landscape Contracting and Estimating Laboratory
courses.description: Calculation of cists, manpower and quantities of materials in landscape development. Preparation of specificationa and estimates used in bidding. Corequisite(s): PLT 4160 .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 131 or PLT 1120 ; and PLT 131L or PLT 1120L .

courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.
